title: What are the three views of a cylinder?
description: A cylinder of radius three centimetres and height eight centimetres stands on its base. The board looks at it from the front, from above and from the side and draws each view. Keeko's doubt is that the front view is a circle.
teaching_notes: One idea: each view is what the eye meets from one direction, so find the outline seen from that direction. Watch for students who draw the round top in the front view.

source: A cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 8 cm stands on its base
video_script.why: The child draws the three views of a solid by looking from each direction in turn, because each view is the outline the eye meets from that direction.
video_script.substitution: cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 8 cm on its base; front view width = diameter = 2 x 3 = 6 cm, height 8 cm, a rectangle; top view a circle of radius 3 cm; side view the same as the front, a 6 cm by 8 cm rectangle.
video_script.anchor: the cylinder standing on its base with an eye at the front, above and at the side
video_script.wrong_answer: the cylinder is round, so the front view is a circle
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko puts a circle in the front view because the solid is round; from the front the eye meets the curved side, a rectangle 6 cm wide and 8 cm tall, and the circle is the view from above, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The front and side views are six by eight centimetre rectangles. The top view is a circle of radius three centimetres

final_answer.value: Front and side views are 6 cm by 8 cm rectangles; the top view is a circle of radius 3 cm
final_answer.spoken: the front and side views are six by eight centimetre rectangles; the top view is a circle of radius three centimetres

hold_back: Front and side views are 6 cm by 8 cm rectangles; the top view is a circle of radius 3 cm
maths_rules: the front view is what the eye meets looking from the front, the top view from above, the side view from the side
front view of the cylinder: width = diameter = 2 x 3 = 6 cm, height = 8 cm, a rectangle
top view: the round top, a circle of radius 3 cm
side view: the same as the front view, a rectangle 6 cm by 8 cm
wrong idea: a round solid does not always give a round view; from the front the eye meets the curved side
video_script.design: One idea: look from each direction in turn. The cylinder stands on the stage and an eye moves to the front, above and the side; each view fills its own frame in the accent colour.
